THE HEADLINES:

 

  1. Government extends services of Agniveers by two years; Also gives nod to 92 Gigawatt-hour energy storage scheme to strengthen country’s clean energy programme.
  2. Union cabinet approves VISTAR Scheme to transform country’s statistical system.
  3. Iran exempts Indian vessels from restrictions on shipping through strategic Strait of Hormuz.
  4. Democrats secure control of both chambers of US Congress in midterm polls, in a blow to President Donald Trump’s Republican Party.
  5. In Hockey, India storm into final of Men’s Asian Championship Trophy beating South Korea, 8-1 in Mohali; To Face Japan in title clash tomorrow.
  6. And in Men’s Cricket, India beat hosts New Zealand by five wickets in rain-hit first ODI of five-match series at Auckland.

Union Cabinet has also approved two year extension of Agniveers who were earlier set to exit after four years of service. Briefing media after the Union Cabinet meeting in New Delhi today, CDS General NS Raja Subramani said, 75 per cent of Agniveers who had to exit will now be given an additional two-year engagement period, after which the willing Agniveers can enrol in the Armed Forces.

  

 

General Raja Subramani said that under the scheme, the remaining 75 percent of Agniveers will now be offered an additional engagement period of two years. He said, upon the completion of this two-year period, all those Agniveers who are willing to continue will be enrolled into the Armed Forces. He said, the extension will come with higher remuneration.

 

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said that the two year extension of Agniveers is aimed at creating a younger, fitter, technologically equipped and future-ready military. In a social media post, Mr Singh said, this will also provide enrollment of all willing Agniveers as regular soldiers after the tenure of 4 or 6 years, who meet the selection criteria.

 

The Union Cabinet has approved 92 Gigawatt-hour energy storage scheme to further strengthen India’s clean energy programme. Briefing media this afternoon in New Delhi, Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vashnaw said, the scheme will comprise 30 Gigawatt-hour of battery storage, 60 Gigawatt-hour of pumped storage and two Gigawatt-hour for emerging energy storage technologies.

 

The Cabinet has also given nod to the ‘Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research, VISTAR Scheme for 2026-27 to 2030-31 with an outlay of over four thousand 371 crore rupees. The VISTAR Scheme is designed to establish a dynamic, real-time and future-ready official statistical architecture for enhanced timeliness, data granularity, interoperability with harmonised and AI ready datasets.  In a social media post, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said that the Cabinet has approved the VISTAR) Scheme to transform India’s statistical system.

The Cabinet has approved the ‘Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing’ with a financial outlay of over two thousand crore rupees over a period of five years. The Prime Minister said that lithium, nickel, and cobalt are essential for EVs, batteries, electronics and defence and India remains heavily dependent on imports of these refined materials.

 

The Cabinet has also approved the continuation of the Centrally Sponsored Scheme for Fast Track Special Courts, including exclusive POCSO Courts, for a further period of five years from 1st April 2026 to 31st March 2031. The Scheme has a total financial outlay of over three thousand 788 crore rupees.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has called for supply chain diversification and greater regional cooperation to strengthen maritime interdependence amid rising security challenges. Mr Singh was addressing the commemorative session of the Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue in New Delhi today. He said the future of the Indo-Pacific would not be shaped by technology alone, but also by how wisely countries use technology, build partnerships and foster mutual trust. He added that India stands ready to contribute to this collective endeavour. The Defence Minister said India’s maritime responsibilities extend beyond its national coastline and that the country has consistently supported an open, inclusive and rules-based maritime order.

The Iranian government today reiterated that Indian vessels are exempt from restrictions imposed on shipping through the strategically important Strait of Hormuz. Iranian lawmaker Ahmad Hayat-Moghaddam, Vice Chairman of the Parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee said India, China, Iraq and Qatar have been granted exemptions and can navigate the waterway without restrictions.

Speaking at a meeting reviewing the country’s economic and security situation, Hayat-Moghaddam said the exemption for India was intended to facilitate the import of essential medicines, while China’s exemption was linked to broader political and economic interests.

Meanwhile, senior Iranian political leaders are reportedly urging the country’s military leadership to consider a diplomatic proposal brokered by Qatar, amid growing fears of a renewed military confrontation with the United States.

In the US, the Democratic Party has secured control of both chambers of the Congress in a sweeping victory in the 2026 midterm elections, dealing a major political setback to President Donald Trump and his Republican Party. In a stunning reversal, Democrats captured the House of Representatives and the Senate, ending Republican control of Congress and setting the stage for a new era of political confrontation in Washington. The elections were held yesterday. 

 

“As per the latest results, Democrats have secured at least 228 seats in the 435-member House of Representatives, comfortably crossing the 218-seat majority mark. In the Senate, they have won 54 seats against 44 for Republicans, with two seats yet to be decided. The counting process is still underway.


The Democratic gains include major victories in traditionally Republican strongholds such as Texas, North and South Carolina, Kansas, Iowa and Ohio, The results signal a strong voter backlash against the Trump administration’s economic and foreign policies.

 

Meanwhile, Indian -American lawmakers have made  a strong mark in the US midterm elections, with four sitting Democratic members re-elected to the House of Representatives and another making her debut in Congress. Ami Bera, RO Khanna, Suhas Subramanyam and Pramila Jayapal have secured  fresh terms while Pia Dandiya made her debut, strengthening Indian-American representation in the US Congress . SWATI RAKHEJA FOR AKASHVANI NEWS.”

The Supreme Court has directed the Centre to constitute a special cell and monitor the implementation of the provisions of the Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2016, which prohibits the employment of child labour in hazardous industries. A bench of Justices SVN Bhatti and NV Anjaria directed the Ministry of Women and Child Development to issue directions to the enforcing agencies through the respective chief secretaries of the States in this regard.

The act imposes a complete ban on child employment and prohibited the employment of children below 14 years in all occupations and processes.

Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush of Diwali and Chhath Puja with extensive crowd management preparations underway at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country.

Our correspondent reports that the facilities have been designed to ensure orderly passenger movement and provide a comfortable waiting environment.

 

“The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Talking to Akashvani News, Northern Railway CPRO Himanshu Kumar Upadhyay said that in New Delhi Railway station, holding area is available for both reserved and unreserved class. He said additional RPF personnel have also been deployed at Railway stations to facilitate passengers.

 

At Anand Vihar Terminal, the Yatri Suvidha Kendra has 14 ticket counters, 16 CCTV cameras, four electronic display boards and seating for 20 passengers. The facility also has separate toilet facilities for male and female passengers, a Divyangjan toilet, an RO plant, 11 HVLS fans and a public announcement system. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing. With Suparna Saikia, Anand Kumar, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

Benchmark domestic equity indices extended their upward momentum for the fifth straight session today.

 

“The Sensex gained 384 points or half a per cent to close at 77 thousand 301. The Nifty added 150 points or 0.63 per cent to settle at 23 thousand 961. In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index surged nearly 1.6 per cent and the Smallcap 100 index climbed two per cent.  Meanwhile, in the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 10 paise to close at 94 rupees and 65 paise against the US dollar. WITH DRISHTI’s Report, ARJUN CHAUDHURI FOR AKASHVANI News.”

The well marked low pressure area which is remnant of Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ over east Telangana and adjoining Coastal Andhra Pradesh is likely to weaken further into a Low Pressure Area during early morning tomorrow.

In Men’s Hockey, the unbeaten India dominantly sealed its berth in the finals of 9th Asian Hockey Championship beating South Korea 8-1 in Mohali this evening. India will face Japan tomorrow in the final at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium in Mohali.

In Men’s Cricket, India have registered a convincing five-wicket victory over hosts New Zealand in the rain-affected first One-Day International at Auckland, taking a 1-nil lead in the five-match series. Put in to bat first, New Zealand were bowled out by India for 185 runs in 40.2 overs. For India, Arshdeep Singh led the bowling attack claiming four wickets. Gurnoor Brar bagged three wickets, while Anshul Kamboj picked up two.

  2. Raksha Mantri Rajnath Singh says modern warfare now extends to space and cyber and digital domains; Says, reforms, self reliance and exports, transformed defence eco-system of the country.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi outlined India’s sustained position as the world’s fastest-growing major economy despite challenging global conditions. The Prime Minister said, earlier, the fight against poverty was only in slogans, today India is defeating poverty on the ground. Mr Modi was speaking after inaugurating and laying foundation stone for various Pune Metro projects worth around 21 thousand 800 crore rupees in Pune today.

 


The Prime Minister said, the commencement of Metro services between Hinjawadi and Shivajinagar will provide improved connectivity to Pune’s major IT hub and offer significant relief to thousands of daily commuters. Highlighting the growth of metro infrastructure in the country, Mr Modi said, India’s metro network has witnessed a major transformation over the past ten to twelve years.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said that the recent conflicts across the world have transformed the character of warfare. He said that the battlefield is no longer confined to land, sea and air but has extended into space, cyberspace and the digital domain. The Defence Minister said this while addressing the third edition of the Delhi Defence Dialogue in New Delhi today. He noted that India’s defence exports have increased from approximately 686 crore rupees in 2013-14 to 38 thousand 424 crore rupees in 2025-26.

 

 

Earlier today, the Defence Minister chaired the meeting of the Consultative Committee of the Ministry of Defence on ‘Modernisation of Indian Defence Forces’ in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan. Emphasising the need for the Defence Forces to remain prepared for present-day and emerging challenges, Mr Singh highlighted the Government’s sustained focus on budgetary support and capital acquisition to meet the modernisation requirements.

 

 

Mr Singh stated that the defence budget for the Financial Year 2026-27 was increased to a record 7.85 lakh crore rupees, including a capital outlay of 2.19 lakh crore rupees earmarked for modernisation and capital procurement.

The Supreme Court today sought responses from the Centre and others on a plea by traders’ organisations seeking a halt to the ongoing protests against the chief election commissioner during the festive season. It said that the protest site cannot be occupied for all times to come. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was hearing several pleas, including one filed by the Kirana Committee Delhi alleging loss of business due to a protest at the Ramlila Maidan.

The Supreme Court Registry today issued a public notice over the creation of a fraudulent domain impersonating its official site and warned all the stakeholders against divulging any personal or financial information. The Registry said, cybercriminals, through the aforementioned link, may attempt to solicit sensitive personal data and confidential credentials of the public. It said, all stakeholders are strictly cautioned against divulging any personal and financial information, as such disclosures may facilitate the theft of data by these fraudsters.

The Ministry of External Affairs has said, the government remains committed to ensuring that Indian students headed to Uzbekistan for medical studies are not exploited. Briefing media in New Delhi this afternoon, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, India continues to engage with Uzbekistan over issues concerning Indian students pursuing education in the Central Asian country.

 

 

On attack on a commercial vessel near Oman, Mr Jaiswal said India is in the process of ensuring that the 13 Indian nationals there are repatriated to India. He said New Delhi is also working to bring the mortal remains of the Indian national who lost his life in the attack.

 

 

<><><> 

 

 

Americans began voting today in one of the most consequential elections in recent times, widely seen as a referendum on Donald Trump’s presidency that has been marked by a prolonged war in Iran, rising inflation and trade wars. At stake in the elections are all 435 seats of the House and 37 seats in the 100-member Senate. The polling will decide whether President Trump’s Republican Party retains control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, the two chambers of the US Congress, or, the Democratic Party wrests control of at least the House if not the Senate, also in the final two years of Trump’s second term in office. Elections are also being held for the post of Governor in 36 states, including in Ohio, where Indian American Vivek Ramaswamy is locked in a keen contest with his rival and Democrat nominee Amy Acton.

The Reserve Bank of India has simplified foreign exchange reporting rules for service exporters and importers, easing compliance requirements for individuals and small-value transactions. A report:

 

 

“Under the revised rules, individuals who export services will no longer have to submit a separate Export Declaration Form, or EDF. They will only need to provide the details of the payment received to their authorised bank. This will be treated as submission of the declaration. The same relaxation will apply to other service exporters for payments received up to ten lakh rupees. The RBI has also simplified reporting requirements for imports of services. Banks will now have to report such transactions only when the importer is not an individual resident in India and the invoice or contract value is more than ten lakh rupees. These changes are expected to reduce compliance requirements for small service transactions and make foreign exchange procedures easier. The revised rules were notified on 2nd November and have come into effect retrospectively from 1st October 2026. sweety Jain,akashvani News, MUmbai.”

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has allowed Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs) to issue depository receipts and list them on GIFT City exchanges, opening up a new avenue for attracting foreign investment. Under the new framework, depository receipts backed by REIT and InvIT units can be listed on India International Exchange and NSE International Exchange at GIFT City. The framework requires approval from at least 75 per cent of unitholders voting in favour of a fresh issue of depository receipts (DRs).

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Bhupender Yadav has reaffirmed India’s commitment to making positive contributions to global efforts towards achieving the objectives of the UN Climate Convention and the goals of the Paris Agreement. Briefing media in New Delhi Today, Mr Yadav said, India will pursue solution-oriented and equitable climate action at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye.

The Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu over south coastal Andhra Pradesh has moved north-north westwards and weakened into a cyclonic storm, and lay centered 40 kilometres west-northwest of Bapatla in Andhra Pradesh. It is very likely to continue to move north-north westwards and weaken into a deep depression today. It is under the continuous surveillance of Doppler Weather Radars at Machilipatnam and Visakhapatnam. A report:

 

 

 

“Heavy rainfall continues in Bapatla, Palnadu, Guntur and Prakasam districts following Cyclone Murasu. The government has stepped up relief, rescue and restoration measures, with more than 45,000 officials and field staff working round the clock. District administrations are closely monitoring rainfall, flood levels and unsafe locations. Special attention is being given to low-lying areas of Bapatla, which may receive floodwater from upper regions of Guntur, Palnadu and NTR districts. Electricity department teams are working to restore power supply in affected areas. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to remain on high alert as rains are expected to continue until tomorrow. He has instructed district collectors to ensure that relief reaches all affected people by tomorrow evening and that the public is regularly informed about rainfall and flood conditions. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

The Indian troika of Ravinder Singh, Saurabh Chaudhary and Amanpreet Singh clinched the team gold in the men’s 50 metre pistol competition in the ongoing ISSF World Championships in Doha today. Ravinder also won the silver medal in the individual competition of the shooting event that is not on the Olympic roster. In Women’s category, Indian trio of Elavenil Valarivan, Sonam Uttam Maskar, and Shambhavi Shravan Kshirsagar bagged silver medal in the 10 metre air rifle team event.

 

India are currently placed second in the table with one gold and two silvers. China are at the top with five medals, including three golds.

Benchmark domestic equity indices surged around 1.6 per cent today, extending their winning streak for the fourth consecutive session. We have a report:-

 

“The Sensex jumped 1 thousand 225 points to close at 76 thousand 918. The Nifty climbed 370 points to settle at 23 thousand 811.

 

 

In the broader market on the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index gained 1.1 per cent and the Smallcap 100 index added 0.3 per cent.

 

 

Meanwhile, in the forex market today, the rupee appreciated by 15 paise to close at 94 rupees and 75 paise against the US dollar. With Ayushi’s’ report Rajesh laikh for Akashvani News”

 

 

Meanwhile, global crude oil prices reversed earlier gains and were trading lower today.

 

 

Brent crude was trading nearly 2.4 per cent down at 102 US dollars and 28 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude was trading 1.6 per cent lower at 94 US dollars and 90 cents per barrel, when reports last came in.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said, the ongoing global crises have highlighted that energy security was directly linked to economic security. He emphasised that the future of energy and economic security lies in clean energy. Mr Modi was addressing the gathering after inaugurating the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi this evening.

 

 

         

Mr Modi said, the global economy faced unprecedented crises over the past few years, ranging from the COVID-19 pandemic to the ongoing crisis in West Asia. He said it is a matter of pride that India, with a population of 140 crore, effectively navigated these global challenges while sustaining high economic growth. He said, the country was firmly progressing towards its target of achieving 500 gigawatts of non-fossil fuel-based energy capacity by 2030.

 

 

 

         

The Prime Minister observed that the next phase of the solar revolution will depend not only on wider adoption but also on innovation.   He stressed the need to bring every government building, school, college, hospital and street-lighting system under solar power.
         

 

Speaking on the occasion, New and Renewable Energy Minister Pralhad Joshi said the sector had attracted investments worth 67 billion US dollars over the past two years.

 

 

         

 

On the occasion, Prime Minister Modi also visited various exhibition stalls and interacted with exhibitors. The theme of the four-day Summit is ‘Invest. Innovate. Inspire’. It is witnessing participation from more than 130 countries, including over 40 ministers.

Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has said, the government will continue to prioritise capital expenditure to sustain India’s growth momentum while ensuring fiscal discipline. Ms Sitharaman was speaking at a private event in Mumbai today. She said capital expenditure had delivered good results over the past four to five years through its multiplier effect and will remain an important part of the government’s growth strategy. She also identified credit access, insurance and pensions as priorities for the next phase of financial inclusion.

Home Minister Amit Shah has directed that Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs) be established in all state capitals by next year. At present, FRRO offices are operational in 20 states. According to the Home Ministry, the number of foreign nationals visiting India for tourism, medical treatment and education has increased substantially, creating the need to expand the FRRO network across the country. The Ministry said, the Central Government is pursuing the establishment of FRROs in the remaining nine states: Bihar, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur and Meghalaya. More from our correspondent.

 

 

         

 

“The establishment of these FRRO offices will help foreigners visiting India in obtaining various consular services such as visa extension, conversion, immigration compliance and legal safety. The expansion will strengthen local-level institutional capacity, improve coordination with State authorities and facilitate legitimate foreign visitors. The Foreigners Regional Registration Office regulates, tracks and facilitates the lawful stay of foreign nationals visiting or residing in India. Overall, the FRRO monitors compliance with Indian immigration laws, handles cases of overstay and visa violations, and coordinates legal action or penalties where necessary. Anand Kumar, Akashvani News Delhi.”

The Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ over the Bay of Bengal is very likely to cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast near Ongole between midnight tonight and early hours tomorrow. IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said, the cyclone will cross Andhra Pradesh coast with wind speeds of 100 to 110 kilometres per hour, gusting up to 120 kilometres per hour, at the time of landfall, bringing heavy rainfall.

 

 

         

 

The governments of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha have stepped up evacuation efforts and disaster preparedness measures to deal with the cyclone.
         

 

Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed all government departments to remain on high alert and take necessary precautionary measures to minimise the loss of life and damage to property. More from our correspondent:

 

 

         

 

“Heavy to extremely heavy rainfall is expected across coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema. Palnadu, Prakasam and Markapuram districts are likely to receive the highest rainfall. Chief Minister N.Chandrababu Naidu reviewed preparedness with senior officials and district collectors. The government has mobilised 724 medical teams, 4,628 emergency beds, 205 relief camps and hundreds of ambulances. Electricity restoration teams, equipment and additional personnel from Chennai are being deployed. Officials have been directed to safeguard tanks and reservoirs, prevent flooding and restore essential services within 48 hours. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea, while people are urged to stay indoors and follow official warnings. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.”

         

 

In Odisha, around one lakh fifty thousand people have been evacuated from vulnerable areas and shifted to shelters and other safer locations. The fresh weather threat comes at a time when several parts of southern Odisha are still struggling to recover from the impact of Cyclone Arnab. Our correspondent has the details:

 

 

         

“Southern Odisha is once again facing a serious weather challenge due to serious cyclonic storm Murasu, particularly in Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Rayagada, Koraput, Malkangiri and Kalahandi. Around one lakh fifty thousand people have been evacuated to cyclone shelters and other safer locations. NDRF and ODRAF teams, along with Fire Services personnel, have been deployed in vulnerable areas to undertake rescue and relief operations. Schools in vulnerable districts will remain closed tomorrow and the day after. With the region still struggling to recover from Cyclone Arnab and the devastating floods, Murasu poses another major challenge for the State administration. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

Ahead of the festival of Diwali, which falls on the 8th of this month, the Supreme Court has permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR during specified hours on the 7th and 8th of November. The apex court further ordered that the complete ban on firecrackers in Delhi-NCR, imposed earlier, will come back into force from the 9th of November.

The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has invoked all measures under Stage Two of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) with immediate effect across the entire National Capital Region. The decision was taken after Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) was recorded at 324 today, placing it in the very poor category. Under Stage Two of GRAP, concerned agencies have been directed to intensify mechanical and vacuum-based road sweeping, along with regular water sprinkling and the use of dust suppressants. The measures also include increasing parking charges to discourage the use of private vehicles.
         

 

The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation has announced that it will operate 20 additional train trips on weekdays from tomorrow following the implementation of GRAP-2 in Delhi.

The Bharatiya Janata Party conducted a “Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao” foot march campaign across the country to counter protests and allegations of the opposition parties. As part of the campaign, Senior BJP leader Amit Shah addressed a massive public rally in Hyderabad. He strongly criticised the Congress party over its recent political rallies, accusing it of attempting to protect illegal infiltrators rather than creating genuine awareness about voter rights. Mr Shah asserted that no illegal infiltrator will be allowed to exercise voting rights.

         

 

The Jharkhand unit of the Bharatiya Janata Party also launched its ‘Loktantra Bachao, Arajakta Hatao’ foot march campaign in Ranchi.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stone of Pune Metro projects worth around 21 thousand 800 crore rupees tomorrow afternoon through video conferencing. These projects will strengthen Pune’s public transportation infrastructure, improve connectivity across the city and provide commuters with an efficient and integrated urban mobility network.

Indian judoka Khushbu Rajakbhai Darjada has assured the country of at least a medal at the Youth Olympic Games at Dakar in Senegal. 15-year-old Khushbu entered the final of the women’s 63-kilogram category, after defeating Algeria’s Dounia Berrahoual. She will now face Germany’s Jolina Reinhold, the reigning Cadet World Champion, in the gold medal match later tonight.
         

 

Meanwhile, Dhinidhi Desinghu has created history by becoming the first Indian female swimmer to qualify for the Youth Olympics final after advancing to women’s 100-metre freestyle medal race.  The 16-year-old from Bengaluru clocked 56.80 seconds to win her heat and finish third overall in the qualifying round.

In the first match of the day, China and Bangladesh played out a one-all draw. In the second match, Japan defeated Malaysia by, 2-1. From Wednesday, the semifinal stage will begin.

Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit outlined his top priorities to strengthen and modernise the Indian Air force a day after taking charge as the 29th Chief of Air Staff. In his first address today, Indian Air Force Chief coined the guiding theme ‘VAYU’, articulating four distinct pillars that will shape the IAF’s future trajectory. These are Vigilance, Victory and Readiness, self-reliance, Yukti, and Unity of Effort. Through the ‘VAYU’ vision, Air Chief Marshal Dixit articulated a clear direction for an operationally ready, technologically advanced, self-reliant and seamlessly integrated Indian Air Force. He emphasised the need to maintain the highest level of operational preparedness across all formations, with restoring combat strength to sanctioned levels being a top priority.

A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal today intensified into a cyclone named as ‘Murasu, prompting Odisha and Andhra Pradesh to step up preparedness for another high-intensity storm in less than a week. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the latest storm is very likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm tomorrow morning.  It is likely to cross south Andhra Pradesh coast as a very severe cyclonic storm between tomorrow midnight to early hours of Tuesday, with wind speeds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph.

 

The IMD has issued a red colour warning for extremely heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh tomorrow. An orange alert has been issued Rayalaseema, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal and Telangana tomorrow.

 

Heavy rainfall is also expected over Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Mahe, Odisha and South Interior Karnataka during the next two days.

Meanwhile, Andhra Pradesh is on high alert, with the state government stepping up precautionary measures to tackle the emerging threat. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

“The deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified into Cyclonic Storm Murasu. It is moving west-northwestwards towards the Andhra Pradesh coast and is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning. It is expected to cross the coast between Nellore and Narsapur during the early hours of Wednesday, with wind speeds of 100 to 110 kilometres per hour. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu reviewed the preparedness and directed departments to coordinate rescue and relief operations. Six NDRF and seven SDRF teams have been deployed. Control rooms have been set up, and evacuation of people from unsafe areas has been ordered. People have been urged to follow official warnings and contact 112 or 1070 for emergencies. Allu Murali, Akashvani News, Vijayawada.“

 

 

Odisha is also preparing for another cyclonic storm, even as thousands of families continue to grapple with the damage caused by Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent floods. As a precautionary measure, authorities have also opened the gates of the Balimela reservoir. We have a report:

 

 

 

“Southern Odisha, still struggling to recover from the devastation caused by Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent floods, is bracing for another spell of heavy rainfall as Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ approaches the neighbouring Andhra Pradesh coast. The India Meteorological Department has forecast rainfall activity in Odisha starting tomorrow, with heavy to very heavy rainfall likely over southern districts on Tuesday and Wednesday. Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Koraput, Nowarangpur and Malkangiri are among the districts requiring close attention, particularly vulnerable hilly areas and flood-prone villages, where fresh rainfall could trigger flash floods and landslides. The state government has identified vulnerable areas, particularly landslide-prone locations, and initiated the evacuation of people to safer places. District Collectors of vulnerable areas have been kept on high alert. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.“

Extreme poverty in the country has declined from 27.1 per cent in 2011 to 2.6 per cent in 2023. The World Bank’s Poverty and Equity report this month has highlighted country’s progress as one of the fastest poverty declines in the world. In a social media post, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that over 49 crore people have moved above the lower-middle-income poverty line during the same period. She mentioned that employment in India also increased by 13.4 crore people between 2017 and 2023, nearly twice the increase in the working-age population. She said that rural women accounted for much of the employment gain, and both rural and urban households experienced substantial welfare gains.

The Finance Minister said, access to electricity reached 99 percent of the population. Ms Sitharaman said the government’s sustained policy efforts are yielding tangible results, strengthening the foundations for inclusive growth and greater economic opportunity.

The Sankosh River has risen by nearly two feet since morning. The river flows along the inter-state boundary between West Bengal and Assam. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

“The precautionary evacuation was carried out on Thursday night following reports of a glacial lake breach in Bhutan, which raised fears of possible flooding in areas along the Sankosh River. Indian Railways has geared up to manage the ongoing festive season rush with extensive crowd management preparations underway at at several railway stations. Ministry of Railways said that Indian Railways is developing dedicated passenger holding areas, known as Yatri Suvidha Kendras, at major railway stations across the country. The Yatri Suvidha Kendras, or Passenger Holding Areas, are being developed to provide dedicated space for unticketed and waiting passengers. More from our correspondent:

 

 

 

“The holding areas have been designed to accommodate passengers before they proceed to the platform area. Udhna railway station in Gujarat is an important example of a station having the modern passenger holding area is especially beneficial for migrant passengers travelling to their hometowns across different parts of the country during the festive season. The facility has been equipped with 10 ticket counters, 120 seats, 55 CCTV cameras, six electronic train display boards, a public announcement system and Wi-Fi connectivity. The aim is to reduce congestion on platforms, in circulating areas and at station approaches by providing designated spaces for waiting and ticketing. Suparna Saikia, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

India’s economic momentum remains strong, with the economy projected to grow by 7.35 per cent in the second quarter of the financial year 2026-27. According to the Finance Ministry’s monthly economic review for October, released today, growth is supported by stronger industrial output, higher energy consumption, increased port traffic, robust GST collections and rising automobile sales. Here is a Report:

 

 

 

“The report highlighted that country’s external sector continued to demonstrate resilience last month amid heightened global uncertainty with total exports of merchandise and services growing by 11 per cent Year on Year. Merchandise exports, which grew by over 23 per cent Year on Year, were the principal driver of this growth, led by electronics and engineering goods. Supported by a steady services surplus, the overall trade deficit narrowed during the period. The report noted that robust domestic demand, sustained investment activity, a resilient financial sector and proactive supply-side management have underpinned India’s growth resilience so far. It said, amidst elevated crude oil prices, higher food inflation and uncertain outlook for the Kharif crop, sustaining economic activity while safeguarding price stability will be the focus of policymakers in the second half of the financial year. Anupam Mishra, Akashvani News, Delhi.”

The Supreme Court has said banks and other financial institutions must be held accountable for losses suffered by victims of digital fraud. The court observed that victims of offences such as digital arrest scams should receive compensation of at least the amount lost if the fraud is found to have resulted from a financial institution’s failure to exercise due diligence. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said, it will examine the Reserve Bank of India’s proposed Know Your Customer (KYC) Amendment Directions, 2026. The directions are expected to be notified by 30th of November and made operational by 31st of December.

World Stroke Day is being observed today to raise awareness about stroke and the importance of recognising its warning signs. This year’s campaign message, ‘Every Minute Counts – Know the Signs of Stroke’, reminds everyone that timely action can save lives.

 

 

On the occasion, Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Jagat Prakash Nadda said, sudden facial drooping, weakness in an arm, or difficulty speaking should never be ignored.

 

 

Talking to Akashvani News, Chief of the Neurosciences Centre at All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, Dr Shailesh B Gaikwad said that the symptoms of the stroke include sudden loss or blurring of vision, double vision, loss of balance, and difficulty in walking. Dr Gaikwad emphasized if such symptoms are visible then the patients should immediately transfer to stroke ready hospital for treatment.

The depression, a remnant of Cyclone Arnab, over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha has moved northwards. It is now centred over central Chhattisgarh and adjoining Odisha. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said it is likely to move further north and weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area over north Chhattisgarh tonight. Meanwhile, IMD has issued a red alert for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in Bihar tomorrow.

 

 

 

In Odisha, torrential rain following Cyclone Arnab has triggered severe flooding and landslides in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts, leaving dozens of villages marooned. More from our Correspondent:

 

 

 

“Incessant rainfall following Cyclone Arnab has affected nearly three hundred villages in Ganjam district, with around 70 reported marooned. More than 2000 people have been stranded, particularly in Sanakhemundi, Aska, Dharakote, Sorada and Patrapur blocks. The Rushikulya river at Purushottampur has risen to 19 metres, above its danger level of 16.8 metres. The Bahuda and Bansadhara rivers are also in spate. Berhampur has witnessed severe waterlogging, while a stretch of National Highway 326 in Gajapati has been washed away, cutting road connectivity. The Indian Coast Guard has begun helicopter evacuations, while rescue teams are assisting affected people. The East Coast Railway has cancelled 20 trains and many other trains have been diverted. The IMD has warned of further rain in Odisha. A new low-pressure area over the South Andaman Sea is likely to intensify into a depression around this Saturday. Prakash Dash for Akashvani News, Bhubaneswar.”

 

 

 

Heavy rain continued across Chhattisgarh today under the influence of Cyclone Arnab. As a precautionary measure, schools in several districts of the state have been closed till tomorrow. A report:

 

 

“Cyclonic storm ‘Arnab’ has weakened into a low-pressure area. It is expected to move towards northern Chhattisgarh over the next twelve hours. As a result, rain is occurring today in several districts across central and northern Chhattisgarh. The Meteorological Department has issued an ‘Orange Alert’ for certain districts within the Surguja, Bilaspur, and Raipur divisions, while a ‘Red Alert’ has been issued for Raigarh and its surrounding areas. In the Bastar division, districts including Sukma have been experiencing rainfall for the past two days. Meanwhile, Union Home Minister Amit Shah spoke with Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai over the phone today to assess the current situation in the state in light of the cyclone. Rahul Sinha, All India Radio News, Raipur.”
